paper.title_en: Observational constraints on viscous free-$γ$ fluid in $f(Q)$ gravity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the late-time cosmological dynamics of a spatially flat FLRW Universe in the framework of exponential $f(Q)$ gravity, where $Q$ denotes the nonmetricity scalar. The matter sector is described by a bulk viscous fluid with a generalized barotropic equation of state characterized by a free parameter $γ$, extending the standard pressureless matter scenario. We derive the modified background evolution equations and investigate the resulting cosmological dynamics. The model parameters are constrained using a combination of cosmic chronometer (CC), DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), CMB, and Type Ia supernova observations. Using the best-fit parameters, we analyze the phase-space dynamics of the model and employ the statefinder and $\mathrm{Om}(z)$ diagnostics to quantify deviations from the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology. We further examine the evolution of the deceleration parameter and the effective equation-of-state parameter, demonstrating a transition from an early matter-dominated decelerating epoch to the present phase of accelerated expansion. Overall, the model provides a viable framework for late-time cosmic acceleration, recovering the standard matter-dominated evolution at early times while naturally evolving toward a stable late-time de Sitter attractor consistent with current observations.
